blocks.text: Design a responsive monitoring UI for one or more training runs. Define lifecycle authority, metric and log volume, snapshot-to-stream continuity, comparison semantics, freshness, and recovery before choosing a transport or chart library.

What you are solving:
A dashboard for a training run that shows live progress (percentage), live metrics (loss/accuracy), and a scrolling log stream.

Decision surface:
- Can you handle realtime updates without UI jank?
- Do you pick a streaming strategy (WS/SSE/polling)?
- Do you model data for charts and logs?
- Do you handle reconnects and stale data?

steps.title: 1. Load run
steps.text: Fetch initial run metadata and render baseline charts.

steps.title: 2. Open stream
steps.text: Subscribe to live updates for metrics and logs.

steps.title: 3. Render updates
steps.text: Update progress bar and charts on a controlled cadence.

steps.title: 4. Handle disconnect
steps.text: Show a reconnect indicator and backoff.

steps.title: 5. Run completed
steps.text: Stop streaming and show final status.

blocks.title: Clarifying questions
items: How often do metrics update (per second, per step)?
Do we need strict ordering for logs?
How many concurrent runs can a user view?
What is the max log volume per run?
Should the dashboard work on mobile?
What happens if the stream drops?

blocks.title: Live-monitoring reliability and accessibility expectations
items: UI should stay smooth under bursty updates.
Charts should not redraw too often.
Logs should be virtualized for large volume.
Reconnect should be automatic and visible.
Stale updates should not overwrite newer ones.

blocks.title: Scope checkpoint
blocks.text: A realtime dashboard is about controlled updates: stream the data, buffer it, and render on a predictable cadence so the UI stays smooth.

The frontend owns run selection, metric normalization, chart windows, lifecycle freshness, comparison state, downsampling, diagnosis views, and accessible summaries. Server-side training execution, checkpointing, and metric authority stay behind abstract snapshot, event, and range-query contracts rather than being implemented here.
